tools.name: doc_new
tools.description: Create a new blank sprite (one transparent layer "Layer 1", one 100 ms frame) and return its document id. Optionally fill it with a background color, pick the color mode, or load a built-in palette. Coordinates everywhere are pixels, 0-based from the top-left; layers and frames are 0-based (layer 0 = bottom of the stack).

background.description: Fill layer 1 with this color (default: transparent).

color_mode.description: Color mode (default rgba). indexed snaps every color to the palette.

palette_preset.description: Load a built-in palette by name (see palette action list_presets), e.g. "PICO-8".

target.description:
Where to create it when the Pixmith app is connected: "app" (default; the sprite opens in a new tab of the app)
or "headless" (kept inside this server only).

tools.name: doc_open
tools.description: Open a file as a new document and return its id plus a summary. Reads Pixmith documents (.pxmt) and Aseprite files (.aseprite/.ase), and imports PNG (one frame), animated GIF (frames + delays), a sprite sheet PNG cut into a grid (give cell_width/cell_height), or a sprite sheet with Aseprite JSON metadata (pass the .json; the PNG named in meta.image is used unless png_path is given), or, with format=trace_grid (File > Import > Trace Pixel Art…), the first image of a file (PNG, JPEG, WebP, ...) traced onto its real pixel grid: "pseudo-pixel" art from AI image tools becomes real pixel art (options pitch auto|n|[x, y], colors, remove_background, shadow, tolerance, global, background_color, close_outline, crop, seed; the result's `trace` has pitch, phase, palette, quality). Imported documents have no .pxmt path yet; doc_save without `path` saves them next to the imported file (same name, .pxmt).

path.description: File to open: .pxmt, .aseprite, .ase, .png, .gif, or a sprite-sheet .json (Aseprite format); with format trace_grid any image.

format.description: How to read it (default auto: by extension; .png with cell_width becomes sheet_grid). native = .pxmt/.aseprite/.ase. (trace_grid: File > Import > Trace Pixel Art…: pseudo-pixel art (AI image tools) traced onto its real pixel grid.)

cell_height.description: sheet_grid: frame height in pixels (default = cell_width).

png_path.description: sheet_json: the sheet image (default: meta.image from the JSON, next to it).

target.description: Where to open it when the Pixmith app is connected: "app" (default; a tab of the app) or "headless".

pitch.description: trace_grid: cell size in source pixels: "auto" (default), a number such as 6.5, or [x, y].

anyOf.description: One cell size for both axes, in source pixels (fractions such as 6.5 are fine).
[x, y] cell size in source pixels.

min_pitch.description: trace_grid, pitch auto: smallest and largest cell size searched (default 3 and 32).

phase.description: trace_grid: [x, y] offset of the first cell edge (default: detected).

separate_axes.description: trace_grid: find the x and y pitch independently.

colors.description: trace_grid: palette: a count, "auto" (default), "keep" or a list of colors.

anyOf.description: A palette of this many colors (k-means), 1-256.
"auto" (the smallest count in min_colors..max_colors that fits, default 2..32), "keep" (no quantising) or "palette" (the sprite's current palette).

items.description: Color as "#RRGGBB" or "#RRGGBBAA" (also "#RGB", "#RGBA", "rgb(r,g,b)", "rgba(r,g,b,a)" with a in 0-1 or 0-255, a CSS basic name like "red", or "transparent"). A fully transparent color erases with the simple ink.

remove_background.description: trace_grid: remove the background (also on when tolerance, shadow, global or background_color is given).

shadow.description: trace_grid, remove_background: also remove a soft drop shadow.

global.description: trace_grid, remove_background: also remove enclosed background-colored pixels.

background_color.description: trace_grid, remove_background: the background color (default: the dominant border color).

close_outline.description: trace_grid: close 1 px breaks in the dark outer outline.

crop.description: trace_grid: crop to the opaque cells (default true).

tools.name: doc_save
tools.description: Save the document. Without `path` it saves to where it was opened/last saved; a document made by an import (PNG, GIF, sheet) and never saved goes next to the imported file (same name, .pxmt), and the result says where. replace=true first closes another open document (an app tab in live mode) that has the target file open, if it has no unsaved changes; with unsaved changes the call fails and nothing is closed. The format follows the extension: .pxmt (Pixmith document, keeps everything) or .aseprite/.ase. Use the export tool for PNG/GIF/sheets. With copy=true it writes a copy and keeps the document's own path and unsaved state.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

path.description:
Destination (.pxmt, .aseprite or .ase). Default: the document's current path; for a document made by an
import (PNG, GIF, sheet) that was never saved: next to the imported file, same name, .pxmt.

copy.description: Write a copy only: the document keeps its path and unsaved state.

replace.description:
Live mode: the Pixmith app refuses to save to a file another tab has open. With replace=true that other tab
(or headless document) is closed first, but only when it has no unsaved changes (otherwise the call fails and
nothing is closed).

tools.name: doc_close
tools.description: Close a document and free it. Refuses when it has unsaved changes unless discard_changes=true. With all_headless=true it instead closes every headless document (ids d1, d2, ...; never the Pixmith app's tabs) at once: documents with unsaved changes are kept and listed unless discard_changes=true. Headless documents also pile up on their own: when more than 32 are open, doc_new / doc_open close the oldest unmodified ones and say so in the result `note`.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

discard_changes.description: Close even if there are unsaved changes (they are lost).

all_headless.description:
Close every headless document (d1, d2, ...) instead of one; the app's documents are never touched. Documents
with unsaved changes stay open (and are listed in `kept_unsaved`) unless `discard_changes` is true. Not
combinable with `doc`.

tools.name: doc_list
tools.description: List the open documents: id, name, path, size, layer/frame counts, unsaved state.

tools.name: doc_info
tools.description: Everything about a document: size, color mode, layer tree (index 0 = bottom; kind image/group/tilemap, visibility, opacity, blend mode, tileset, iso grid and offset of isometric tilemaps, tween parent/terrain data, user data), frames and durations, which cels have pixels or are linked, tags, palette, slices, tilesets, sprite user data, selection, free-transform/floating state, undo history size and the active layer/frame defaults. Use `sections` to fetch only parts of it.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

sections.description: Parts to include (default: all). The summary (size, mode, counts) is always included.

tools.name: doc_set_active
tools.description: Set the document's active layer and/or frame: the defaults every tool uses when `layer`/`frame` are omitted (Lua scripts see them as activeLayer/activeFrame). New layers and frames become active automatically.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

layer.description: Layer index or name to make active.

tools.name: app_status
tools.description: Tell whether the Pixmith app is running and connected (live mode): app version and front end, its open documents (ids app:<id>) and the active one, plus the headless documents kept inside this server. When connected, tools edit the app's documents and the user sees every edit appear in the window, each one an undo step "AI: <tool>"; otherwise they edit headless documents (ids d1, d2, ...). Call it first when unsure where an edit will land.

tools.name: app_connect
tools.description: Connect (or reconnect) to a running Pixmith app on this computer, for example after starting it, and return the same information as app_status. With several instances running the newest is used unless `pid` picks one. Errors when no app is running or the app has live mode switched off in its Preferences.

pid.description: Process id of the app instance to use (see app_status); default: the newest running one.

tools.name: app_disconnect
tools.description: Disconnect from the Pixmith app and work headless until app_connect is called. The app's documents stay open in the app; headless documents (ids d1, d2, ...) are unaffected.

tools.name: game_screenshot
tools.description: Take a screenshot of the running Godot game and return it as an image (plus its size and the game's client name as JSON). Needs live mode (Pixmith 0.5.1 or later running) and a game started from Godot in debug with the Pixmith Live Link addon enabled (see export_godot). After editing a sprite, call this to see the result in the game itself: Live Link has already put the new art into the running game. Pixel-art games are small, so `scale` (integer 1-8, nearest neighbour, long side capped at 2048 px) enlarges the picture. Errors when no such game is running or it does not answer within `timeout_ms`.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for the game's frame, in milliseconds (default 3000, at most 10000).

scale.description: Integer upscale 1-8 for small pixel games (default 1); nearest neighbour, the long side stays within 2048 px.

annotations.title: Screenshot of the running Godot game

tools.name: render
tools.description: Render the sprite as a PNG image you can look at (MCP image content). Defaults: the active frame, all visible layers composited, scaled up so the long side is about 512 px, on a light checkerboard so transparency is visible. Options: other frames (up to 16 images at once), a single layer or group in isolation (shown even if hidden), a region, an explicit integer scale, a solid/transparent background, and Onion Skin (onion_skin: neighboring frames tinted red = before, blue = after) and View > Frame Difference (diff_prev=true: pixels that changed from the previous frame tinted over the render, magenta = changed, green = appeared, red = disappeared; diff_opacity, diff_wrap, diff_layer; see also the frame_diff tool for counts). The app's Grid, Isometric Grid, Tiled Mode and Preview are view-only and are not drawn. Never changes the document. For exact colors use get_pixels.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

frame.description: Frame to render (default: the active frame).

frames.description: Several frames, one image each (max 16). Overrides `frame`.

layer.description: Render only this layer (index or name; a group renders with its children), even if hidden.

region.description: Only this rectangle of the canvas.

scale.description: Integer upscale 1-64 (default: auto, long side about 512 px; output is capped at 4096 px).

before.description: Frames before the current one to show (tinted red). Default 1.

after.description: Frames after the current one to show (tinted blue). Default 1.

opacity.description: Opacity of the onion frames, 0-1. Default 0.35.

onion_skin.description: Show neighboring frames faintly (off by default).

diff_prev.description: Frame Difference: tint the pixels that changed from the previous frame over the render (magenta changed, green appeared, red disappeared). Off by default.

diff_wrap.description: diff_prev: the frame before frame 0 is the last frame (default true; false = frame 0 has no reference).

diff_layer.description: diff_prev: compare only this layer's cel instead of the composite (the app's "Active layer only").

tools.name: frame_diff
tools.description: View > Frame Difference as numbers (and optionally an image): which pixels a frame changed compared with the frame before it, to find parts of a character that "stuck" or tore during a walk cycle (onion skin shows where the previous frame was, this shows what did not move with the rest). Counts `changed` (visible in both frames but a different color or alpha), `appeared` (transparent before), `disappeared` (transparent now), their `total`, `bounds` {x, y, w, h} around all of them (null when the frames match) and `reference_frame` (the frame compared against). The frame before frame 0 is the last frame when wrap=true (default; right for looping animations), none when wrap=false (then every count is 0). Compares the composite of the visible layers, or only the cel of `layer` (hidden layers count). Give `frames` or all=true for a table over many frames without images; image=true returns the difference tinted over the frame (magenta changed, green appeared, red disappeared). `render` with diff_prev=true draws the same overlay on any render. Never changes the document.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

frame.description: Frame to compare with the one before it (default: the active frame).

frames.description: Several frames: one result row each, no image (max 4096). Overrides `frame`.

all.description: Every frame of the document (a table of rows, no image).

layer.description: Compare only this layer's cel (index or name) instead of the composite of the visible layers.

wrap.description: The frame before frame 0 is the last frame (default true; false = frame 0 has no reference).

image.description: Also return the difference tinted over the frame as an image (a single frame only).

tools.name: get_pixels
tools.description: Read exact pixel colors of a rectangle, from the composited image or from one layer's cel (raw cel pixels, before layer/cel opacity). The default `legend` format gives one string per row with one character per pixel plus a legend mapping characters to #rrggbbaa colors (and palette indices) — compact and easy to reason about; `hex` gives a 2-D array of colors. At most 16384 pixels per call (4096 for hex); page through larger areas.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

layer.description: Read one layer's cel (index or name). Omit for the composited image of all visible layers.

region.description: Rectangle to read (default: the whole canvas, if small enough).

tools.description: The Eyedropper (color picker): read the color at one pixel: the composited color plus the value of every layer that has a non-transparent pixel there (top first), and the palette index if the color is in the palette.

tools.name: brush
tools.description: Custom brush (Brush from Selection / Reset Brush): `capture` turns the selected pixels of a layer into the brush used by every later drawing call (until `reset`); `info` reports it. The brush is shared by all documents.

doc.description: capture: document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

layer.description: capture: layer to take the selected pixels from (default: active).

tools.name: select
tools.description: Change the selection (one undo step each): rect (Rectangular Marquee: x, y, w, h), lasso (Lasso: freehand outline points), polygon (Polygonal Lasso: corner points), wand (Magic Wand at x, y with tolerance; contiguous by default), by_color (Select by Color: every pixel matching the color at x, y), iso_tile (Select > Isometric Tile: the diamond cell of an isometric grid, by a pixel x, y or by col, row; the grid is the active isometric tilemap layer's (or `layer`'s) when there is one, else the document's iso_grid settings, default 32x16 at 0, 0; or give tile_w, tile_h, offset_x, offset_y), all, none, invert, expand/contract/border (by `amount` pixels). mode = replace (default), add or subtract combines with the existing selection. Also edits the selected pixels: delete (clear them), move_pixels (the Move tool: shift the selected pixels by dx, dy), crop (crop the canvas to the selection bounds). Returns the selection bounds. Drawing and filters only affect selected pixels while a selection exists; select none to remove it.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

mode.description: replace (default), add or subtract — for rect, polygon, lasso, wand, by_color, iso_tile (the app's Shift = add, Alt = subtract).

x.description: rect: left; wand/by_color: sample point x.

y.description: rect: top; wand/by_color: sample point y.

col.description: iso_tile: cell column (with row); alternative to x, y.

tile_w.description: iso_tile: tile width in pixels, even, 4-4096 (default: the isometric layer's cell, else the iso_grid setting, else 32).

tile_h.description: iso_tile: tile height in pixels, even, 4-4096 (default: the isometric layer's cell, else the iso_grid setting, else 16).

offset_x.description: iso_tile: x of the grid's cell (0, 0) (default: the isometric layer's offset, else the iso_grid setting, else 0).

offset_y.description: iso_tile: y of the grid's cell (0, 0) (default: the isometric layer's offset, else the iso_grid setting, else 0).

layer.description: Layer sampled by wand/by_color and edited by delete/move_pixels (default: active); iso_tile: the isometric tilemap layer whose grid to use.

tools.name: iso_grid
tools.description: Read or set the isometric grid of a document: tile_w x tile_h (even, 4-4096; default 32 x 16) and offset_x / offset_y (where cell (0, 0)'s bounding box starts; default 0, 0). Cell (col, row) has its box at (offset_x + (col - row) * tile_w / 2, offset_y + (col + row) * tile_h / 2). `select` action iso_tile uses these as its defaults, so set the grid once. When the document has an isometric tilemap layer (tilemap add_layer with cell_w; Tilemap iso) the grid IS that layer's: iso_grid get reports its cell size and offset (`source` "layer"; the layer is `layer`, else the active layer if it is isometric, else the only isometric layer), set moves the layer's grid offset (offset_x / offset_y; the cell size comes from its tileset, see tileset action set_iso) and select iso_tile uses it by default, so the overlay, the tilemap and the selection share one offset. Without an isometric layer the settings are kept by this server for the document (not in the file or in the app: the app's Isometric Grid view settings cannot be read or written through the live protocol) and are lost when the server stops or the document is closed. Actions: get (default), set (only the fields you give change), reset (forgets the server's setting).

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

offset_x.description: set: x of cell (0, 0)'s bounding box.

offset_y.description: set: y of cell (0, 0)'s bounding box.

layer.description: The isometric tilemap layer whose grid to read or move (default: the active layer if isometric, else the only isometric layer).

tools.name: clipboard
tools.description: Edit > Cut / Copy / Paste (clipboard shared by all documents): copy or cut the selected pixels of a layer (the whole canvas when nothing is selected); paste them (or a PNG file with paste_image) as a floating selection at (x, y) (default: where they were copied from); move the floating pixels by (dx, dy) like the Move tool; commit to drop them onto the layer, or cancel to discard the paste. A floating paste is also committed by the next edit.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

layer.description: Layer to copy from / paste into (default: active).

x.description: paste/paste_image: left edge (default: the copied position, or 0).

dx.description: move: horizontal offset of the floating pixels.

tools.name: transform
tools.description: Edit > Flip Horizontal / Flip Vertical / Rotate 90: flip or rotate the selected pixels, or the whole cel when nothing is selected: flip_horizontal, flip_vertical, rotate_cw / rotate_ccw / rotate_180 (exact 90-degree turns), or rotate by any `angle` in degrees (clockwise) with RotSprite resampling (keeps pixel-art edges crisp; rotsprite=false for nearest neighbour). all_frames / all_layers repeat it over frames / layers, all in one undo step.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

layer.description: Layer (default: active).

all_frames.description: Apply to every frame of the layer.

all_layers.description: Apply to every image layer of the frame(s).

tools.name: free_transform
tools.description: The Free Transform tool (Edit menu) for the selection (or cel): begin, then set any of x, y, width, height, angle (degrees), skew_x, skew_y (the preview updates; `anchor` picks the fixed point for width/height), read the state with info, and commit (one undo step) or cancel. Any other edit also commits it.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

layer.description: begin: layer (default: active).

rotsprite.description: begin/set: RotSprite resampling for rotation (default true).

anchor.description: set: the point that stays fixed when width/height change (default center).

tools.name: sprite_size
tools.description: Sprite > Canvas Size and sprite scaling: resize the whole sprite (all layers and frames): `scale` resamples the pixels (nearest neighbour) to width x height (or by `factor`); `canvas` changes the canvas size without scaling, placing the old image by `anchor` (default center) or explicit offset_x/offset_y (where the old top-left lands; negative crops).

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

factor.description: scale: multiply both sides by this (e.g. 2 or 0.5) instead of width/height.

anchor.description: canvas: where the old image sits in the new canvas (default center).

offset_x.description: canvas: explicit x of the old top-left in the new canvas (overrides anchor).

offset_y.description: canvas: explicit y of the old top-left.

tools.name: warp
tools.description: Edit > Warp…: bend, stretch or nudge part of a cel like a puppet, without blur and without new colors. A `grid` of [cols, rows] handles (each 2-8, default [2, 2]) is spread over the selection bounds (the whole canvas when nothing is selected); `offsets` has one [dx, dy] per handle, row by row from the top-left (cols * rows entries; the content at that handle moves by that many pixels), interpolated bilinearly or, with smooth=true, with a Catmull-Rom spline. `pins` ([{x, y, dx, dy, radius}], up to 32) move the content within `radius` of a canvas point by up to (dx, dy), fading out smoothly. The result is resampled by majority vote (`samples` points per output pixel along each axis, 1-8, default 4): nothing is blended. Only selected pixels are read or changed. One undo step; returns changed=false when no pixel moved. The result lists the handle positions (`handles`, canvas coordinates) so you can aim the offsets. preview=true returns an image of the frame with the warp applied and changes nothing. Very thin 1 px diagonals can break under a strong bend.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

layer.description: Layer (default: active).

offsets.description: One [dx, dy] per handle, row by row from the top-left (cols * rows entries; default all zeros).

samples.description: Sample points per output pixel along each axis, 1-8 (default 4).

smooth.description: Interpolate between handles with a Catmull-Rom spline instead of bilinearly.

x.description: Canvas x of the pin (pixel corners are integers).

dx.description: How far the content at the pin moves along x.

dy.description: How far the content at the pin moves along y.

radius.description: Content within this many pixels is affected, fading out towards the edge.

preview.description: Return an image of the warped frame and change nothing.

tools.name: layer
tools.description: Layer menu and panel: edit the layer stack (index 0 = bottom; a group comes right below its children in the list). Actions: add (new image layer above `layer`, default above the active one), add_group, duplicate, remove (alias: delete; a group with its children), move_up / move_down (one step), move_to (to stack position `to`), into_group (move into `group`), out_of_group, wrap_in_group (put the layer in a new group), merge_down, set (any of name, visible, opacity 0-255, blend_mode), import_sheet (slice a sprite-sheet PNG `path` into cells of cell_width x cell_height (cell_height defaults to cell_width), read row by row, onto consecutive frames of the existing image `layer` (or a new one with new_layer=true and `name`) starting at `frame` (default 0); frames are created after the last one as needed; optional cols / rows / frames limit the cells; one undo step), import_png (PNG file as a new layer; with replace=true it instead puts the PNG into the existing `layer` at `frame` in one undo step, keeping the layer's name, order, opacity and blend mode, optionally shifted by x / y). New layers become the active layer. Returns the updated layer list.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

layer.description: The layer to act on, index or name (default: active). For add/add_group/import_png: the new layer goes above it.

import_png: true replaces the pixels of the existing `layer` (default: active) at `frame` with the PNG, as ONE
undo step, instead of adding a new layer. The layer keeps its name, position, opacity and blend mode (a cel
that was linked to other frames becomes independent). `name` renames the layer. The cel becomes exactly the
PNG on a transparent canvas.

import_png with replace: canvas x where the PNG's left edge goes (default 0; may be negative; the PNG is
clipped to the canvas).

y.description: import_png with replace: canvas y where the PNG's top edge goes (default 0).

tools.name: frame
tools.description: Frame menu and timeline: edit animation frames (0-based). Actions: add (`count` empty frames after `frame`, default after the active one), duplicate (copy `frame` right after itself, `count` times in one undo step and, in live mode, one request to the app; link=true makes the copies share the source's cels instead of copying pixels, so many copies cost almost no memory; unlinked copies cost frames x layers x canvas size), remove (alias: delete), move (frame `frame` to position `to`), set_duration (milliseconds for `frame`, `frames` list, or every frame with all=true). Tags are adjusted automatically.

duplicate: share the source frame's cels with the copies (linked cels, like `cel link`) instead of copying
the pixels, so N copies cost almost no memory and the document stays small. Editing one copy edits them all
until `cel unlink`. Default false.

tools.description: Edit cels (the image of one layer in one frame). color.description: Tag color in the timeline (alpha ignored).

tools.name: palette
tools.description: Read or edit the document palette (0-based indices; one undo step per call). Actions: get, set (entry `index` to `color`; in indexed mode pixels using it follow), add (append `colors`), insert (`color` at `index`), remove (`indices`; alias: delete), move (`indices` to before `to`), duplicate (`indices`), replace_all (the palette becomes `colors`), sort (by hue or luminance), ramp (insert `steps` blended colors between entries `index` and `to`, in RGB or HSV), from_sprite (palette of the colors used, optionally quantized to max_colors), list_presets, load_preset (`name`), load_file / save_file (`path`, GIMP .gpl or .hex).

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

items.description: Color as "#RRGGBB" or "#RRGGBBAA" (also "#RGB", "#RGBA", "rgb(r,g,b)", "rgba(r,g,b,a)" with a in 0-1 or 0-255, a CSS basic name like "red", or "transparent"). A fully transparent color erases with the simple ink.

hsv.description: ramp: blend in HSV instead of RGB.

max_colors.description: from_sprite: quantize to at most this many colors (default: exact, up to 256).

tools.name: color_mode
tools.description: Convert the sprite's color mode: rgba, grayscale, or indexed (every pixel snapped to the palette; `dither` 2/4/8 uses an ordered Bayer dither instead of nearest color). conform_only=true re-snaps all pixels to the current mode without converting (after editing the palette, say).

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

tools.name: filter
tools.description: Apply an FX filter to a cel (default), every frame of a layer (target=layer) or every layer of a frame (target=frame), limited to the selection's bounds when something is selected or to `region`. Kinds and their parameters: replace_color (from_color, to_color, tolerance), invert, desaturate, hsl (hue -180..180, saturation and lightness -100..100), brightness_contrast (brightness, contrast -100..100), color_balance (red, green, blue offsets -255..255), outline (color, inside, eight_connected), drop_shadow (dx, dy, color), remove_isolated_pixels (eight_connected), blur, sharpen (3x3, alpha-aware), curves (curve_rgb / curve_red / curve_green / curve_blue / curve_alpha: [[x, y], ...] control points in 0-255), clean_edges (FX > Clean Edges…: tidy a sprite traced from reference art, never touching interior detail such as eyes, 1 px highlights or fingers; passes halo [halo_rings, halo_gain, halo_saturation], despeckle [pieces smaller than N pixels that touch the outside], holes [fill enclosed transparent areas smaller than N], light_specks, thin_outline [thickness, outline_color, outline_tolerance, outline_luma]; name no pass to run halo + despeckle + thin_outline with their defaults, otherwise only the passes you name run; use the read-only `lint` tool to see what is wrong first), remove_background (FX > Remove Background…: make the paper background transparent by flood fill from the border: tolerance 0-255 default 28, shadow [also a soft drop shadow, shadow_depth 1-95 percent], global [also enclosed background-colored pixels], color [background color; default the dominant border color]). preview=true returns an image of the result and changes nothing; with `region` the image is cropped to that region (the result says so).

layer.description: Layer (default: active).

preview.description: Return a preview image instead of applying (cropped to `region` when given).

shadow.description: remove_background: also remove a soft drop shadow connected to the background.

shadow_depth.description: remove_background: how much darker than the background a shadow may be, percent 1-95 (default 55).

global.description: remove_background: also remove background-colored pixels enclosed by the figure (eyes, windows).

halo.description: clean_edges halo pass: remove light, grayish paper-halo pixels from the outer rings (true, or give halo_rings).

halo_rings.description: clean_edges: rings to peel, 1-8 (default 2); names the halo pass.

halo_gain.description: clean_edges: how much lighter than what is behind a halo pixel must be, luma 0-255 (default 40); names the halo pass.

halo_saturation.description: clean_edges: halo pixels are at most this saturated, percent 0-100 (default 30); names the halo pass.

despeckle.description: clean_edges despeckle pass: remove loose pieces smaller than this many pixels that touch the outside (default 4; 0 = off).

holes.description: clean_edges: fill enclosed transparent areas smaller than this many pixels (0 = off; a transparent eye is a hole too).

light_specks.description: clean_edges: also replace a lone light pixel whose 8 neighbors are all much darker (a 1 px highlight in a dark eye looks like this).

thin_outline.description: clean_edges: thin a dark outer outline of 2..thickness pixels to 1 pixel (true, or give thickness).

curve_rgb.description: curves: master RGB curve points [[x, y], ...].

scale.description: preview: integer upscale of the image (default auto).

tools.name: lint
tools.description: FX > Lint Sprite…: inspect a cel (default), every frame of a layer (target=layer) or every layer of a frame (target=frame) and report problems without changing anything. Per cel and category a count (always complete) and a capped list of positions {x, y, size} (0-based pixel coordinates; for an area its first pixel in scan order and its pixel count). Categories: light_edge (light, grayish paper-halo pixels on the two outermost rings), holes (enclosed transparent areas), specks (small pieces detached from the body, `speck` pixels or fewer), no_outline (edge pixels that are not outline-colored and have no outline neighbor), strays (a pixel unlike all 8 neighbors), semi_transparent (0 < alpha < 255), off_palette (colors missing from the palette; only with palette=true). Fix halos, specks and thick outlines with `filter` kind clean_edges.

tools.name: trace
tools.description: File > Import > Trace Pixel Art… on a cel of an open document: "pseudo-pixel" art (AI image tools: upscaled soft edges, a drifting grid, noise, paper-white background, drop shadow) becomes real pixel art. Finds the grid pitch and phase (pitch auto, or a number / [x, y] in source pixels), takes the median color of each cell, snaps to a palette (colors: a count, "auto", "keep", "palette" = the sprite's palette, or a list of colors), optionally removes the background and shadow (remove_background, shadow, tolerance, global, background_color), closes 1 px breaks in the dark outline (close_outline) and crops to the opaque cells (crop, default true). The chosen cel defines the grid, palette and crop and every image cel of the document is resampled with them, so an animation stays on one grid; the canvas becomes the traced size (one undo step). Returns width, height, pitch, phase, palette, quality (0-1), origin, grid_cells, closed_outline and the background report. preview=true returns the traced picture as an image, detect_only=true only the pitch and phase; neither changes anything. To trace straight from a file into a new document use doc_open format=trace_grid. Needs an RGB sprite without tilemap layers.

max_pitch.description: pitch auto: largest cell size searched (default 32).

"auto" (the smallest count in min_colors..max_colors that fits, default 2..32), "keep" (no quantising) or "palette" (the sprite's current palette).

items.description: Color as "#RRGGBB" or "#RRGGBBAA" (also "#RGB", "#RGBA", "rgb(r,g,b)", "rgba(r,g,b,a)" with a in 0-1 or 0-255, a CSS basic name like "red", or "transparent"). A fully transparent color erases with the simple ink.

remove_background.description: Remove the background from the traced cells (also on when any of tolerance, shadow, shadow_depth, global or background_color is given).

shadow.description: remove_background: also remove a soft drop shadow.

shadow_depth.description: remove_background: how much darker than the background a shadow may be, percent 1-95 (default 55).

global.description: remove_background: also remove enclosed background-colored pixels.

background_color.description: remove_background: the background color (default: the dominant border color).

close_outline.description: Close 1 px breaks in the dark outer outline.

crop.description: Crop to the opaque cells (default true).

preview.description: Return the traced picture as an image and change nothing.

detect_only.description: Only find the grid (pitch and phase) and change nothing.

tools.name: tileset
tools.description: Work with tilesets (tile index 0 is always the empty tile). Actions: list, image (see every tile as one picture, labeled grid in index order), get_tile (pixels of one tile in the legend format), set_tile (replace a tile's pixels from `rows`+`legend` or a PNG `path`), add_tile (append an empty tile, or one with pixels), duplicate_tile, delete_tile (alias: remove_tile; cells using it become empty, higher indices shift down), rename, set_base_index (the number shown for tile 1). Isometric tilesets (Tilemap iso): set_iso {cell_w, cell_h} makes a tileset isometric (cell_w 0 makes it square again; only while no layer shows its tiles), get_pivot / set_pivot {tile, pivot: [x, y]} / clear_pivot (the pivot is the point of the tile image, from its top-left corner, that sits on the center of the diamond; the default is centered and, for images taller than the cell, bottom-aligned so the diamond is the bottom cell_h rows), pivots (every tile's pivot, custom ones marked) and texture_origin {tile?} (the pivot as Godot's TileData.texture_origin, offset from the image center, which export_godot_tileset writes). Drawing on a tilemap layer also edits the tiles it shows.

action.description: set_iso: Isometric tilesets: make a tileset isometric (or square again).

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

tileset.description: Tileset index or name (default: the tileset of the active layer, else 0).

rows.description: set_tile/add_tile: one string per row, one legend character per pixel (as returned by get_tile).

additionalProperties.description: Color as "#RRGGBB" or "#RRGGBBAA" (also "#RGB", "#RGBA", "rgb(r,g,b)", "rgba(r,g,b,a)" with a in 0-1 or 0-255, a CSS basic name like "red", or "transparent"). A fully transparent color erases with the simple ink.

legend.description: set_tile/add_tile: character -> color; "." is transparent unless mapped.

path.description: set_tile/add_tile: PNG file with the tile's pixels (tile-sized).

cell_w.description: set_iso: diamond cell width in pixels (even; 0 makes the tileset square again).

cell_h.description: set_iso: diamond cell height in pixels (default cell_w / 2).

pivot.description: set_pivot: [x, y] point of the tile image, from its top-left corner, that sits on the center of the diamond.

tools.name: tilemap
tools.description: Tilemap layers: add_layer (new tilemap layer + tileset with tile_width x tile_height tiles, above `layer`), convert (turn an image layer into a tilemap, deduplicating tiles; flip_aware shares flipped copies), to_image (back to a normal layer), assign_tileset (use another tileset of the same tile size), stamp (the Tile Stamp mode: place `tile` at canvas pixel x, y, optional flip_x / flip_y / diagonal; tile 0 clears), get_tile, grid (the layer's tile indices as rows, read-only). Isometric tilemaps (Tilemap iso; 2:1 Godot DIAMOND_DOWN diamonds): add_layer with cell_w, cell_h (default cell_w / 2), layout diamond_down and offset [x, y] (the canvas pixel of cell (0, 0)'s box, e.g. cell 96 x 48 at offset [592, 360]) makes an isometric layer: cell (i, j) has its box at (offset_x + (i - j) * cell_w / 2, offset_y + (i + j) * cell_h / 2), i running down-right and j down-left; tile images (tile_width x tile_height, default the cell size) may be taller than the diamond (cliffs, tufts) and overlap the cells behind them. On iso layers stamp / get_tile take the cell `i`, `j` (or a canvas pixel x, y, which is turned into its cell; get_tile with x, y also reports the front-most visible tile `seen`), grid lists cells (rows = j, columns = i) and `offset` gets or sets the layer's grid offset, which is how layers at other elevations are placed (a ledge half a cell up is the floor's offset minus cell_h / 2 in y). The terrain tools and terrain_paint work on iso layers (modes sides and blob; canvas pixel points are mapped to cells).

action.description: offset: Isometric layers: get or set the grid offset.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

layer.description: The tilemap layer (default: active). add_layer: the new layer goes above it.

flip_aware.description: convert: flipped/rotated copies share one tile.

x.description: stamp/get_tile: canvas pixel x inside the cell.

y.description: stamp/get_tile: canvas pixel y inside the cell.

tile.description: stamp: tile index (0 clears the cell).

name.description: add_layer: name of the new layer.

cell_w.description: add_layer: makes an ISOMETRIC layer: the diamond cell width in pixels (even; e.g. 96). Default tile_width = cell_w.

cell_h.description: add_layer (iso): the diamond cell height (default cell_w / 2). Default tile_height = cell_h.

layout.description: add_layer (iso): the cell layout (only diamond_down). (diamond_down: Godot TILE_LAYOUT_DIAMOND_DOWN (the only layout).)

offset.description: add_layer (iso) / offset: [x, y] canvas pixel of cell (0, 0)'s bounding box (default [0, 0]); offset without it reads the offset.

i.description: stamp/get_tile: the cell column i (with j) instead of a canvas pixel; on iso layers cell (i, j) is the diamond at offset + ((i - j) * cell_w / 2, (i + j) * cell_h / 2).

j.description: stamp/get_tile: the cell row j (with i).

tools.name: terrain
tools.description: Set up terrain auto-tiling on a tilemap layer (Godot-compatible peering). Modes: sides (16 tiles, N E S W), blob (47 tiles, sides + corners), corners (dual grid, 4 corners). Actions: create (first terrain + mode), set_mode, add / remove (alias: delete) / edit / move (terrain priority), list, generate_template (append a labeled template tileset for the mode; reduced = only flip/rotation representatives), assign_masks (give tiles 1.. the template's masks in order), set_tile (a tile's mask / terrain / peers / symmetry / weight), get_tile, set_options (edge_same, seed), rebuild (recompute every cell), clear_overrides, missing (cells that had no matching tile, read-only report). Paint with terrain_paint. Works on isometric tilemap layers too (modes sides and blob; the dual-grid corners mode needs square tiles; generate_template draws diamond-shaped templates at the tiles' pivots).

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

layer.description: Tilemap layer (default: active).

color.description: create/add/edit: terrain color (for display and Godot).

mask.description: set_tile: neighbor mask (sides: N=1 E=2 S=4 W=8; blob: N=1 NE=2 E=4 SE=8 S=16 SW=32 W=64 NW=128; corners: TL=1 TR=2 BR=4 BL=8); -1 removes the tile's terrain data.

peers.description: set_tile: terrain of each ring direction, e.g. {"n": 1, "e": 0} (n ne e se s sw w nw; 0 = empty).

symmetry.description: set_tile: allowed symmetries bitmask (1 flip X, 2 flip Y, 4 diagonal).

weight.description: set_tile: random weight among tiles with the same mask.

edge_same.description: set_options: cells outside the map count as the same terrain.

seed.description: set_options: random seed for weighted variants.

tools.name: terrain_paint
tools.description: The terrain brush: paint terrain with the auto-tiling brush on a tilemap layer (the right tiles are chosen from the masks): paint (canvas pixel `points`, optional brush_size/round/mirror), rect (x, y, w, h), flood (fill the connected area at x, y), erase (paint terrain 0), override (force `tile` at x, y; 0 removes the override), pick (read the terrain at x, y). One undo step per call. On isometric layers the canvas pixel positions are mapped to diamond cells through the layer's grid offset.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

layer.description: Tilemap layer (default: active).

terrain.description: Terrain id (1-15) or name to paint (paint/rect/flood).

mirror.description: Symmetry: none, horizontal, vertical or both.

tile.description: override: tile index to force (0 removes the override).

tools.name: slice
tools.description: The Slice tool and Slice Properties: named rectangles exported with sprite sheets and used for UI 9-patches and pivots. Actions: list, add (name, bounds), set (any of name, bounds, center = the 9-patch middle rectangle relative to the slice, pivot = [x, y] relative to the slice; clear_center / clear_pivot remove them), remove (alias: delete). Bounds, center and pivot are keyed per frame: a value set at `frame` applies from there until the next key (default frame 0).

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

center.description: set: 9-patch center rectangle, relative to the slice's top-left.

pivot.description: set: pivot [x, y] relative to the slice's top-left.

frame.description: Frame the bounds/center/pivot key applies from (default 0).

tools.name: user_data
tools.description: Read or set the user data (text and color, as in Aseprite) of the sprite, a layer, a cel, a tag or a slice. Writing to an empty cel creates it.

action.description: get (default when nothing is given to set) or set.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

layer.description: layer/cel target: layer (default: active).

tag.description: tag target: tag index or name.

slice.description: slice target: slice index or name.

text.description: set: text ("" clears; omitted keeps the current text).

tools.name: tween
tools.description: Animate a layer (or group) by keyframes instead of redrawing it: properties x, y (offset in pixels), rotation (degrees, clockwise), scale_x, scale_y (1 = 100%), opacity (0-1). Between keys the value follows the key's ease: linear, hold, in_quad, out_quad, in_out_quad, in_out_cubic, out_back, out_bounce, or bezier with control points [x1, y1, x2, y2]. Actions: info (keys, pivot, options, the transform at `frame`), set_key, set_keys (several properties at one frame), remove_key (alias: delete_key), move_key, set_ease, set_pivot / reset_pivot (rotation/scale center), set_options (rotsprite, snap_scale, ignore_opacity), copy_keys / paste_keys, bake (render the tween into real cels: mode all / range / frame; new_layer puts them on a new layer; keep_source keeps the keys), bake_all. Tween rig (the app's Tween panel Parent picker): a layer can have a tween parent, so its transform is the parent's composed with its own about its own pivot: rotate a thigh and the shin, whose pivot is the knee, follows (thigh -> shin -> boot, body -> arm). Actions set_parent (parent = a layer; fails for a cycle, a group or a tilemap), clear_parent, get_parent, children (direct children of `layer`), composed_transform (at `frame`: matrix [a, b, c, d, e, f] with x' = a*x + c*y + e, y' = b*x + d*y + f including all ancestors, rotation in degrees, scale_x, scale_y and where the layer's pivot is on the canvas; a child without keys of its own just follows its parent). Opacity is not inherited. info shows parent, children and the effective frame range. bake and bake_all are rig-aware (a child bakes with its composed transform; baking a child alone detaches it; a layer that still has children needs keep_source or bake_all). The parent link is saved with the document. Tweened layers already render and export animated; bake when you need real per-frame pixels to edit.

action.description: set_parent: Tween rig: give the layer a parent.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

layer.description: Layer or group (default: active).

frame.description: Key frame (default: active); info: frame to evaluate; paste_keys: where to paste; bake mode frame: the frame.

ease.description: Ease from this key to the next (default linear).

bezier.description: bezier ease: [x1, y1, x2, y2] (like CSS cubic-bezier).

to.description: move_key: destination; copy_keys/bake range: last frame.

snap_scale.description: set_options: round scale to whole multiples.

parent.description: set_parent: the parent layer (index or name).

new_layer.description: bake: put the baked cels on a new layer (groups always do).

keep_source.description: bake: keep the keys and the source cel.

tools.name: export
tools.description: Export to image files (the document itself is not changed; use doc_save for .pxmt/.aseprite). format: png (one frame, `frame` counts within the exported frames), gif and apng (animated, frame durations kept), png_sequence (`path` is a base name; writes <base>-001.png, ...), sheet (sprite sheet PNG; layout horizontal / vertical / grid with `columns`, padding, border, extrude, json=true also writes Aseprite-style JSON metadata next to it). Options: scale (integer upscale), tag (export only that tag's frames, apply_direction expands reverse/ping-pong), split_tags (one file per tag), layers (visible / single `layer` / each layer to its own file), trim (none / per_frame / uniform), ignore_empty. dry_run=true only reports how many files it would write.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

path.description: Output file (png_sequence: base name without extension). Split exports add "-<layer>-<tag>" to the name.

tag.description: Only this tag's frames (index or name).

apply_direction.description: Expand the tag direction (reverse, ping-pong) into the frame order (default true).

layers.description: visible (default): layers as shown; single: only `layer`; each: every visible layer to its own file.

layer.description: layers=single: the layer (default: active).

trim.description: none (default), per_frame (crop each frame to its content), uniform (one crop for all frames).

ignore_empty.description: Skip frames with no visible pixels.

border.description: sheet: margin around the sheet (default = padding).

extrude.description: sheet: repeat each frame's edge pixels this many times (against texture bleeding).

json.description: sheet: also write the Aseprite JSON metadata (<name>.json).

dry_run.description: Only report how many files would be written.

tools.name: export_godot
tools.description: File > Export to Godot: export a Godot 4 SpriteFrames resource (.tres, one animation per tag, durations kept) plus its atlas PNG(s), optionally an AnimatedSprite2D scene (.tscn), into a Godot project. `project_root` is the folder containing project.godot and `tres_path` must be inside it. Re-exporting keeps resource uids stable. Without project_root/tres_path the settings saved in the document are used (save_settings=true stores the ones you pass). preview=true writes nothing and returns the .tres text, the files it would write and the first atlas page as an image. Live Link: export once with save_settings=true so the document knows its res:// resource; after that a game running the Pixmith Live Link addon (godot/addons/pixmith_live_link in the Pixmith repository, debug builds only) updates its sprites after every edit, including edits made through this server, with no re-export or restart. Call game_screenshot to look at the running game. Live Link and the game view need the Pixmith app 0.5.1 or later.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

project_root.description: Godot project folder (contains project.godot). Default: the document's saved settings.

tres_path.description: Output .tres path inside the project. Default: the document's saved settings.

extrude.description: Repeat edge pixels into the padding.

trim.description: Crop frames to their content (offsets keep them in place).

per_animation_png.description: One PNG per animation instead of one shared atlas.

name_template.description: File stem template: {name} is the .tres stem, {layer} the layer name.

layers.description: Layers to include by name (default: visible layers).

save_settings.description: Store these settings in the document (saved with it) for later re-exports.

preview.description: Describe the export without writing anything.

tools.name: export_godot_tileset
tools.description: File > Export Tileset to Godot: export a tileset as a Godot 4 TileSet resource (.tres) with its atlas PNG, including the terrain set and peering bits from terrain auto-tiling (or `mode` when there is none), flipped alternatives and optional collision shapes; write_scene=true also writes a .tscn with TileMapLayer nodes painted from the document's tilemap layers. Isometric tilesets (Tilemap iso) export as tile_shape ISOMETRIC / tile_layout DIAMOND_DOWN with tile_size = the diamond cell, every tile's pivot as its texture_origin, peering bits turned to Godot's isometric names and no flipped alternative tiles; the scene positions each isometric TileMapLayer at the layer's grid offset (its elevation) with y_sort_enabled so tall tiles overlap the cells behind them. preview=true describes the export without writing (the core's description plus a `tileset` block: tile_shape, tile_layout, tile_size, cell and image sizes, a texture_origin summary and the isometric scene layers with their positions).

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

tres_path.description: Output .tres inside the project (relative paths are relative to project_root).

mode.description: Terrain mode when the layer has no auto-tile data: blob (default), corners, sides.

collision.description: none (default), full (tile square) or polygon (traced from opaque pixels).

extrude.description: Edge pixels to replicate around each tile.

write_scene.description: Also write <name>.tscn with TileMapLayer nodes painted from the tilemap layers.

terrain_name.description: Terrain name when there is no auto-tile data (default: the tileset name).

terrain_color.description: Terrain color when there is no auto-tile data.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo the last `steps` edits (default 1). Every mutating tool call is one undo step (or one per transaction).

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

tools.name: redo
tools.description: Redo `steps` edits that were undone (default 1). Any new edit after an undo clears the redo steps.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

tools.name: history
tools.description: List the undo history: applied steps (oldest first, with labels such as "Pencil" or "Filter: Blur") followed by undone steps that can be redone, and the current position. Use undo/redo or history_goto to move.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

offset.description: First step to list (default: so that the last `limit` steps show).

tools.name: history_goto
tools.description: Undo or redo until exactly `position` steps are applied (0 = the document as opened/created; see history).

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

position.description: Number of applied steps to end up with.

tools.name: transaction
tools.description: begin: start a transaction so every following tool call on this document becomes part of ONE undo step named `label` (e.g. a whole character drawn with many calls); end: close it. Transactions nest; end every begin. Undoing while a transaction is open is not allowed.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

label.description: begin: name of the undo step (default "Edit").

annotations.title: Group edits into one undo step

tools.name: run_lua
tools.description: Run a Lua 5.4 script against a document (sandboxed: io / os / app.fs / file loading and saving only inside `allow_paths`, everything else is denied; 128 MB memory, 10 s by default, `timeout_seconds` 1-120 raises the time and the instruction budget with it; source up to 16 MiB) as ONE undo step; if it raises an error the document is left unchanged. The script sees `sprite` (pixels, layers, frames, cels, tags, slices, tilesets, selection, palette, user data), `app` and `color`; print() and app.alert() output is returned. NOTE: in Lua, layers/frames/tags are 1-based (layer 1 = bottom) while pixel coordinates and palette indices are 0-based; `sprite.activeLayer`/`activeFrame` are the document's active layer/frame. Files: with `allow_paths` (folders inside --root or an --allow-dir) a script can read images and sprites (`Image{ fromFile=... }`, `Sprite{ fromFile=... }`, `app.open(path)`) and write files; the script can see only ITS document plus the sprites it opens or creates itself (`app.sprites` lists exactly those): documents open in this server or in the Pixmith app are NOT visible to it, so doc_save (copy=true) the other document into an allowed folder and app.open it, or move pixels with clipboard / cel copy. Sprites a script creates or opens come back as new headless documents. Read the full API with the help tool (topic lua_api) or the pixmith://docs/lua-api resource. Give `source` (aliases: `script`, `code`) or a .lua `path`.

doc.description: Document id (see doc_list); optional when only one document is open.

path.description: A .lua file to run instead of `source`.

timeout_seconds.description: Time limit in seconds, 1-120 (default 10). The instruction budget grows in proportion.

allow_paths.description:
Folders (or files) the script may read and write with io / os / app.fs / Image{fromFile} / app.open /
saveAs. Everything else is denied (there is nobody to ask). Must be inside the server's --root.

tools.name: help
tools.description: Documentation for using this server: guide (conventions and workflows — read this first), lua_api (the full Lua scripting reference for run_lua), lua_examples (example scripts shipped with Pixmith), palettes (palette and color mode tools, built-in preset names), tools (one line per tool), app_tools (every tool of the Pixmith app - Pencil, Eraser, Paint Bucket, Blur, Marquee, Isometric Tile, ink modes, ... - mapped to its MCP call), and short how-tos per tool group: documents, layers, drawing, selection, transform, filters, cleanup (trace, lint, clean edges, remove background, frame difference, warp), tilemaps (incl. isometric), slices, tween (incl. the parent rig), export, history, live.

guide (default), lua_api, lua_examples, palettes, tools, app_tools (the Pixmith app's tools/menu items mapped to MCP calls), or a tool group: documents, layers, drawing, selection,

instructions:
# Pixmith MCP: how to use it

Pixmith is a pixel-art editor (sprites, animation, tilemaps; .pxmt and .aseprite files). This server runs its
engine in-process; every tool call edits real documents with the same code the desktop apps use.

## Conventions
- Documents have ids ("d1", "d2", ...) from doc_new / doc_open (in the Pixmith app: "app:<id>", see Live mode).
  `doc` may be omitted when only one is open (with the app connected: the app's active document).
- Files: with --root every path must be inside it; --allow-dir folders (e.g. a temp dir) additionally take reads and export output.
- Pixel coordinates are 0-based from the top-left. Rectangles are {x, y, w, h}; shape corners are inclusive.
- Layers are 0-based with 0 at the BOTTOM of the stack; a group appears right below its children. Layers can
  also be addressed by exact name. Frames are 0-based. (Lua scripts are 1-based for layers/frames/tags.)
- Tools without `layer`/`frame` use the document's active layer/frame; new layers/frames become active.
  doc_set_active changes them. Check doc_info when unsure.
- Colors: "#RRGGBB" or "#RRGGBBAA" (also "#RGB", "rgb(...)", CSS basic names, "transparent"). Results print
  "#rrggbbaa". The default "simple" ink replaces pixels; a transparent color erases.
- Headless documents pile up: close them with doc_close (all_headless=true closes them all); past 32 open ones the
  oldest unmodified are closed automatically and the result `note` says so.
- Every mutating call is exactly one undo step (undo / redo / history). Wrap a multi-call edit in
  transaction begin/end to make it one step. Failed calls change nothing.
- While a selection exists, drawing, fills, gradients and filters only touch selected pixels. select none clears it.

## Live mode (the Pixmith app)
- When the Pixmith app is open on this computer, the tools edit ITS documents: the user watches every edit appear in
  the window, and each call is one undo step named "AI: <tool>" that they can take back with Cmd/Ctrl+Z. Without
  the app everything works headless, in documents kept inside this server (ids "d1", "d2", ...).
- app_status tells which one you have: connected or not, the app's documents (ids "app:<id>", e.g. "app:doc-3") and
  the active one. app_connect / app_disconnect switch at runtime (use app_connect after the user starts the app).
- In live mode `doc` may be omitted to mean the app's ACTIVE document, so the user chooses the target by switching
  tabs. doc_new / doc_open create the sprite in the app (target "headless" keeps it inside the server instead);
  doc_save / doc_close / doc_set_active act on the app's tab. doc_list shows both kinds.
- Once the app has been connected in this session, a call that creates or edits a document never silently turns
  headless: if the app is gone it reconnects once and otherwise returns an error. Start the app again, pass
  target "headless" (doc_new / doc_open) or a headless `doc` id, or call app_disconnect to work headless on purpose.
- Tools default to the app's current layer and frame; aiming a tool at another layer or frame moves the app's
  current one there, so the user sees where you are working. The user may edit at the same time: a call that lost
  that race is repeated on the new version automatically, and a busy app (open dialog) is retried for a few seconds.
- Not available on app documents: history, history_goto (the app owns the undo history; transaction does nothing,
  every call is its own step). undo / redo work when the app supports them and otherwise tell the user to press
  Cmd/Ctrl+Z. The app's own selection is not visible to tools; a selection made with the select tool lives in this
  server until someone else changes the document.
- Prefer a few meaningful calls over thousands of tiny ones: every call is a full round trip to the window and an
  undo step. draw_pixels (batches), draw_polygon and run_lua are good for bigger drawings.

## Looking at your work
- render returns a PNG you can see (auto-scaled, checkerboard = transparent). Render after each meaningful step.
- get_pixels returns exact colors as a character grid + legend (great for checking outlines and palettes).
- doc_info lists layers, frames, cels (which have pixels), tags, palette, slices, tilesets, selection, history.

## Typical workflows
- New sprite: doc_new (width, height, optionally palette_preset) -> palette (load_preset / replace_all) ->
  layer add (e.g. "outline", "color") -> draw_* / fill -> render -> doc_save path=... .pxmt or .aseprite.
- Animation: draw frame 0 -> frame duplicate -> edit the new frame -> repeat -> frame set_duration ->
  tag add (name, from, to, direction) -> render frames=[...] or onion_skin to compare -> export gif / sheet.
- Tween instead of redrawing: tween set_keys at two frames (x/y/rotation/scale/opacity, ease); render and
  exports show the motion; tween bake turns it into editable cels.
- Tilemap: tilemap add_layer (tile size) -> draw tiles via tileset set_tile or by drawing on the layer ->
  tilemap stamp. Auto-tiling: terrain create (mode) -> terrain generate_template -> paint the template
  tiles -> terrain assign_masks -> terrain_paint paint/rect/flood -> terrain missing to check coverage.
- Sprites traced from AI reference art: doc_open format=trace_grid (or trace on an open cel) puts pseudo-pixel art on a real
  grid; filter remove_background / clean_edges tidy it; lint lists what is still wrong; frame_diff / render diff_prev find
  walk-cycle parts that did not move; warp bends a cel without blur. Help topic cleanup.
- Isometric maps: tilemap add_layer with cell_w, cell_h, offset (e.g. 96 x 48 at [592, 360]) -> tilemap stamp {i, j, tile} ->
  tileset set_pivot for tall tiles -> terrain / terrain_paint -> export_godot_tileset (ISOMETRIC / DIAMOND_DOWN). Help topic tilemaps.
- Godot: export_godot (project_root with project.godot, tres_path inside it; one animation per tag) and
  export_godot_tileset for tilesets with terrains. preview=true shows what would be written.
- Godot Live Link (Pixmith app 0.5.1 or later): export_godot once with save_settings=true; then a running game with the
  Pixmith Live Link addon (debug builds) updates its sprites after every edit you make, no re-export. game_screenshot
  returns a screenshot of that running game (scale 1-8 enlarges small pixel games) so you can check the result.
- Replace one layer's pixels from a PNG in one undo step: layer action import_png with replace=true (path, layer, frame,
  optional x / y). More how-tos per tool group: help topics app_tools (the app's tool names), documents, layers, drawing, selection,
  transform, filters, cleanup, tilemaps, slices, tween, export, history, live.
- Anything else: run_lua (see help topic lua_api); timeout_seconds (1-120) allows longer scripts.
